title: Doc Club
content: Doc Club jmyllarn@helsinki.fi Wed, 14/10/2026 - 09:47 Doc Club is a monthly seminar organised by our research group, where doctoral researchers are given the opportunity to present their research and receive feedback from the audience. Sessions are mostly hybrid to give an opportunity to meet peers face-to-face and to enable participation remotely when needed.

title: AI can help run factories better: University of Helsinki thesis sharpens the 3D models
content:
Digital twins are virtual 3D replicas of real spaces such as factories, warehouses and industrial plants. Companies use them to monitor equipment, plan maintenance and simulate changes without disrupting operations. 

For a digital twin to be genuinely useful, the system has to understand what each object in the scene actually is: which part is a pipe, which is a container, which is a machine. Identifying and labelling those objects is known as the segmentation problem.

Ofia Rahman Alif's thesis examines this problem. The work was funded by the project, which supports the adoption of artificial intelligence in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). 

The research was carried out in collaboration between the University of Helsinki's and , a Finnish company that builds digital twins of complex industrial facilities.

title: LekaMed continues – Focus on democratic education, participation and agency
content:
How can adults and children together create a more democratic everyday environment in early childhood education and pre-primary education? is one of the questions explored during the project this autumn. Throughout the autumn, Marina and Sara are working closely with a pre-primary education group and its staff to explore this and related questions. 

Alongside the collection of research data, staff are supported in their professional development in matters related to democratic education, participation, and agency. Material developed in collaboration with Petra Holm at Moilo is being tested together with staff in the group, while different approaches to creating a more democracy-promoting everyday environment are also being explored. 

Through this collaboration, we aim to develop approaches and practices that can be shared with other professionals working in early childhood education. The goal is to contribute to a culture in which children can experience democracy and where children’s voices are given genuine space and taken seriously, says Marina.

title: Anwar Arifin’s Weavers of the Distant Past, Part 2
content:
Anwar Arifin is a doctoral researcher in economic anthropology. As a member of the WORK-IT project, he is currently researching about the historiography of the Ancient Near East, and what kind of assumptions are born from modern social, political, and economic theory that influence the way scholars perceive and produce the history of the Ancient Near East.

Which sources have mattered most to you, and how has it been to obtain and integrate them without a background in historical research or methodological training?

title: Palkittu geenitutkimus selvitti long Covid -oireyhtymän riskitekijöitä
content:
Some people experience persistent symptoms for months or even years after a coronavirus infection. This condition is known as long COVID. Common symptoms include debilitating fatigue, brain fog and respiratory problems.

One of the key findings of the award-winning study was that genetic susceptibility to long COVID is linked to the regulation of lung function. In particular, the FOXP4 gene emerged as an important factor, helping researchers better understand the cellular mechanisms underlying long COVID.

The study was led by Hanna M. Ollila, a group leader at the Institute for Molecular Medicine Finland (FIMM), University of Helsinki.

The interdisciplinary study analysed genetic data from more than one million people across 16 countries. In Finland, the researchers used data from FinnGen, which includes more than half a million biobank participants.

According to Ollila, the findings highlight the importance of FinnGen and other population-based studies in understanding chronic conditions that develop following infections.
